refresh: Yearly, after the IRS (October/November) and Minnesota Department of Revenue (December) publish the next year's figures. Dollar thresholds are in tax-year dollars; the engine deflates income to today's dollars before applying them, which treats them as inflation-indexed. Social Security taxation thresholds and the NIIT threshold are fixed in law (not indexed) and are applied in nominal dollars.
sources: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 inflation adjustments, incl. One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes): MFJ standard deduction $32,200; 0% long-term capital gains rate to $98,900 MFJ.

Minnesota Department of Revenue, 2026 brackets and standard deduction (Dec 2025): MFJ 5.35% / 6.80% / 7.85% / 9.85% at $48,700 / $193,480 / $337,930; standard deduction $30,600; Social Security subtraction in full at AGI up to $110,780 MFJ.
SSA 2026 PIA bend points $1,286 and $7,749; IRS 2026 elective deferral limit $24,500.

single.note: Estimated: 2025 single figures indexed by the MFJ bracket change (about 2.3%).

early_withdrawal.note: Pre-tax withdrawals before 59 1/2 (integer ages: before 60) pay the 10% penalty. The rule of 55 and 72(t) payments are not modeled, so early-retirement results are conservative.

working_years.note: Flat rates for withdrawals while still working (e.g. college shortfalls): gains at 15% federal + 3.8% NIIT + about 7.85% MN; pre-tax at 24% federal + 7.85% MN + 10% penalty.
